research_question: What source-independent evidence supports historical-modern continuity between Steffel participial -ameke/-ame and modern participial/derivational -ame/-ami/-kame/-nami domains?
major_revision_from_v2: SRC-02 provenance is unresolved and likely belongs to a pre-2016 Hilton lexicographic lineage, so SRC-02/Hilton overlaps are no longer counted as independent replications.
Hilton 1959 and revised 1993 are treated as one editorial lineage; Shoemaker 2016 is an explicit update of that line.
The 1997 Compendio adds independent multivariety speaker-level evidence for -kame/-kami/-name/-nami/-ame/-ami color morphology.
Hill 2020 remains comparative support, but its Rarámuri cochí datum derives from Hilton 1959 and is not counted as a separate Rarámuri witness.
Candidate strength is now graded by independent source families rather than raw document count.

publication_level_claim_v3: Steffel provides source-explicit historical participial -ameke and ke-loss variation; Merrill analyzes relevant historical chains with participial -(a)me plus optional final -kV/-ke; independent modern grammars and multivariety data document participial -ame/-kame and surface -ami/-kami/-nami systems. After controlling for Hilton/SRC-02 documentary dependence, several lexical and color-domain comparisons still survive with independent modern Rarámuri support. This supports a structured continuity hypothesis for a participial/derivational domain, not a universal one-step sound change from -ameke to -ami.
methodological_rules: Count independent source families, not document totals.
Keep critical analysis separate from lexical attestation.
Treat SRC-02/Hilton overlap as potentially dependent until provenance is resolved.
Treat Hilton 1959/1993 and Shoemaker 2016 as one editorial lineage for independence counting.
Use Compendio 1997 and Caballero 2022 as independent modern Rarámuri evidence where relevant.
Treat Hill's Rarámuri item as Hilton-derived while retaining its external Uto-Aztecan comparative value.
Do not equate historical -ame-ke with modern -ka-me without independent morphological evidence.
Preserve superseded versions and negative controls.
